## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga that forms free-floating colonies composed of groups of four cells connected by fine, branching strands derived from the mother-cell wall. Dimorphococcus lunatus has two characteristically different cell shapes within each group: inner cells are generally cylindrical or oval, while outer cells are more kidney- or heart-shaped. It occurs in freshwater habitats including ponds, lakes, wetlands, and bog waters and has a broad worldwide distribution, including the southeastern United States. Like other planktonic green algae, it contributes to primary production and forms part of the base of freshwater food webs.
